facts.text: The user asked whether Gottlob Frege, Leonard Bloomfield, and Wilhelm Wundt made contributions to the study of word meanings.
The user requested examples from Gottlob Frege's papers "On Sense and Reference" and "The Thought" to illustrate Frege's view on word meanings.
The user stated that Gottlob Frege distinguished between sense (Sinn) and reference (Bedeutung) of an expression.
The user stated that, according to the sense/reference distinction, sense is the mode of presentation or the way a referent is conceived.
The user stated that, according to the sense/reference distinction, reference is the object to which the expression refers.
The user stated that Frege's work on the philosophy of language, particularly in "On Sense and Reference" and "The Thought," made groundbreaking contributions to the study of word meanings.
The user requested examples from Leonard Bloomfield's work "Language" to illustrate Bloomfield's view on word meanings.
The user stated that Leonard Bloomfield's book "Language" emphasized a scientific, systematic approach to the study of language.
The user stated that Bloomfield focused on observable elements of linguistic structure.
The user stated that Bloomfield considered meaning to be an element of linguistic structure.
The user stated that Bloomfield believed meaning could not be studied directly because it was inherently subjective and tied to individual experience.
The user stated that Bloomfield proposed that linguists should focus on the objective study of form and function in language.
The user stated that Bloomfield's approach laid the groundwork for later developments in structural and formal semantics.
